original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove that every rational decomposition 2I = R+S+T into nonzero symmetric rank-one matrices is first-order character-excluded, and therefore the all-old-once seven-call profile (a,b,p,q,r,s,t)=(1,1,1,1,1,1,1) admits no word.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the three-frame question left open by the two-signed-frame floor, for the single all-old-once count profile.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. The profile still needs eight paid calls, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after the all-old-once three-frame character proof or an explicit rational survivor. Do not search the other twenty census profiles or four-or-more frames.
evidence: Elementary character proof for every rational rank-one solution of R+S+T=2I: the parity image in F2^2 avoids (1,1), so an AB or PQ form extends, and that form detects two calls and four targets. The scale formula is an expanded polynomial identity. Finite fixtures and the mod-8 discriminant check are in verify.py. The inherited first-order call inequality is not reproved.

open_questions.question: Which of the other twenty three-frame count profiles from the seven-call census survive the first-order character test?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only (1,1,1,1) with three added labels used once is settled here. A surviving profile would be the next place a seven-call word could exist.
open_questions.first_step: Take one other census profile, write its determinant equation, and test the same AB/PQ obstruction on one rational rank-one solution.
open_questions.blocked_by: No uniform reduction from those profiles to R+S+T=2I is supplied.

open_questions.question: Can four or more added signed rank-one frames lower the eight-call minimum?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two-summand sign reduction and this three-summand character both stop at the number of added frames they assume.
open_questions.first_step: Fix four primitive directions and the shortest determinant equation that uses each new label once, then repeat the parity-image test.
open_questions.blocked_by: No four-frame support or character reduction is supplied.
